children: Gentherm plans to issue 2.9 million additional shares and declare a special dividend as part of its deal to merge with Modine's spin-off.

Modine's board plans to record the spin off its performance technologies business on Sept. 28, with the distribution of the spin-off's stock slated for Oct. 1. Gentherm then plans to merge with the company that same day.
The companies first announced the deal in January.

Each Modine shareholder as of Sept. 28 will receive one share of the spun-off company for each Modine stock they own on the day of the distribution. After the acquisition, each share of the spun-off company will convert to a right to receive a number of Gentherm shares equal to the exchange ratio.

The agreement provides a mechanism to preserve the tax-free nature of the deal, which includes the potential adjustment of the exchange ratio to be used at closing to determine how many Gentherm shares should be issued for each share of the spun-off company.

The companies expect the exchange ratio will be increased under the adjustment provisions in the deal. As a result of the increase in the ratio, Gentherm expects to issue about 2.9 million additional shares as part of the merger.

To offset the value of the shares issuance, the cash distribution paid by the spun-off company prior to the merger will be reduced to $159 million from $210 million. Gentherm will also pay a special dividend.
The special cash dividend of $1.90 a share, or roughly $58.4 million in aggregate.

The dividend is contingent on the acquisition and will be payable on Oct. 7 to shareholders of record as of Sept. 28. Modine shareholders who receive shares of Gentherm stock as part of the deal won't be entitled to the dividend.
Immediately prior to the merger closing, Gentherm shareholders are expected to own about 56% of the combined company. Former holders of the spun-off company's stock are expected to own about 44%.
